**2B.10 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Overall read: **negative**. There were some narrow diplomatic positives, especially on Rohingya repatriation and defensive border management, but Hasina’s 2024 record ended with lethal domestic repression, a legitimacy crisis, and international alarm. On balance, Bangladesh’s regional/international posture looks **less peaceful, less stable, and less lawful** by year-end than at the start.

**Accepted claims**

- **PM Hasina reiterates call to China to help repatriate Rohingyas to Myanmar**
  - **Publisher:** TBS News / UNB
  - **Date:** July 10, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar-895921
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina pushed a diplomatic track for Rohingya repatriation through talks with Myanmar and support from China. This is a real positive: it shows one inherited regional conflict being handled through diplomacy rather than force.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh said it would not admit more Rohingya because supporting the existing population threatened its own security**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** February 7, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-will-not-let-in-any-more-rohingya-refugees-minister/1958020/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh justified a refusal to take more Rohingya as a defensive security necessity. This is consistent with a managed, constrained regional posture rather than destabilizing cross-border conduct.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh ramps up border vigilance as thousands of Rohingya flee Myanmar**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** September 11, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-ramps-up-border-vigilance-as-thousands-of-rohingya-flee-myanmar/2262488/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh tightened border vigilance amid renewed violence in Myanmar and refugee flows. This is a defensive, stabilizing move, not evidence of regional coercion.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to global disarmament at UNGA**
  - **Publisher:** BSS
  - **Date:** October 9, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.bssnews.net/news/215175
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh called for decisive collective action against nuclear threats and stressed peaceful uses of nuclear energy. This supports a more lawful and peace-oriented international posture.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 1B.4, 1B.2

- **Convention on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons : draft resolution**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations Digital Library
  - **Date:** October 11, 2024
  - **URL:** https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4064553
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh is listed as an author of a UN draft resolution prohibiting the use of nuclear weapons. That is strong evidence of legalistic, de-escalatory international behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 1B.4, 1B.2

- **Reducing nuclear danger : draft resolution**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations Digital Library
  - **Date:** October 11, 2024
  - **URL:** https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4064552
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh is listed as an author of a draft resolution aimed at reducing nuclear danger. This reinforces the picture of a state trying to support rules-based restraint.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 1B.4, 1B.2

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com
  - **Date:** July 22, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-calm-a-day-after-top-court-scrapped-some-job-quotas-3528153
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed opponents for the violence instead of moving toward compromise. This domestic coercion weakened Bangladesh’s international standing and made the broader posture less lawful and stable.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** July 20, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters described internet/text shutdowns and a nationwide curfew as the government escalated. That is strong evidence against a more peaceful or lawful posture and contributed to international concern.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations / OHCHR
  - **Date:** July 26, 2024
  - **URL:** https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights
  - **Claim-level summary:** The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This is the clearest indicator that Bangladesh’s 2024 internal conduct worsened lawfulness and stability rather than improving them.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 2B.4, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigns, interim government to be formed**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** August 5, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-resigns-interim-government-to-be-formed/2208572/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported Hasina fled and an interim government would be formed. The year ended in institutional collapse, which is hard to square with a more stable or lawful regional posture.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

**Synthesis**

- **Positive:** Hasina/Bangladesh did pursue some genuine diplomacy on Rohingya repatriation and maintained a defensive line on border management and nuclear restraint.
- **Negative:** Those positives were narrow. The broader 2024 record was dominated by coercive domestic repression, rights abuses, international condemnation, and regime collapse.
- Best-supported conclusion: **No, Hasina did not leave Bangladesh’s regional/international relations more peaceful, stable, and lawful than she inherited them.** The year’s end state was more volatile and internationally discredited, even if a few diplomatic tracks remained active.

**Search gap**

- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** of a major improvement in Bangladesh’s relations with neighbors or international institutions beyond the limited Rohingya and nonproliferation diplomacy above.
- I also found **no credible evidence** of a large external-war or interstate escalation agenda in 2024; the main damage to international standing came from the domestic crackdown and resulting legitimacy crisis.
